# Dedup benchmark fixture

`records.ndjson` (55 schema-conformant strata records) and `labels.json`
(ground truth) implement the labelled benchmark
openspec:deduplication#validation-against-a-labelled-benchmark requires. Generated by
`scripts/generate_dedup_benchmark_fixture.py` -- re-run that script after
editing the data it contains, rather than hand-editing the `.ndjson`/`.json`
files here.

## Why synthesised, not ASySD or `revtools`

openspec:deduplication#validation-against-a-labelled-benchmark names ASySD and `revtools` as "suitable public benchmarks." This
environment has no live internet access to fetch either dataset or verify
its licence terms before redistributing a derived copy in this repository,
so the fixture here is synthesised instead, following the same provenance
convention as `tests/fixtures/exports/` (see `tests/fixtures/SOURCES.md`):
every record is hand-authored by the strata project, and where a title,
author list, or journal matches a real published paper that is deliberate
(it makes the fixture realistic and independently checkable), but no byte of
this fixture is copied from any real database export or from ASySD/`revtools`
itself. If a maintainer with access to one of those datasets wants to swap
or extend this fixture with it later, `strata.dedup.benchmark.compute_metrics`
and `scripts/dedup_benchmark.py` are already dataset-agnostic -- only
`load_fixture()`'s two file reads would need to point elsewhere.

## Structure

`records.ndjson`: one CSL-JSON-shaped strata record per line, `id`s
`rec_bm00000000000001`..`rec_bm00000000000055`, grouped in three blocks (see
the generator script's `_CLUSTERS`/`_CONFUSABLE_PAIRS`/`_NOISE` for the exact
membership):

1. **Duplicate clusters** (2-3 records each): the same underlying work as it
   might be re-exported by different databases (Scopus, Web of Science,
   PubMed, Embase, EBSCOhost, Crossref, or a manually-entered record), with
   realistic cross-database variation -- DOI present on both/one/neither
   side, title case and punctuation, abbreviated vs. expanded journal names,
   full page ranges vs. first-page-only, online-first vs. print year
   (off by one), and an author-particle case (`van der Meer`). One cluster's
   DOI matches exactly on both sides (the fast-path score of 1.0); the rest
   exercise the weighted formula.
2. **Confusable pairs** (4 pairs): deliberately hard *true negatives* --
   two different works that share enough (author, year, journal, volume, or
   near-identical title tokens) to be proposed as a blocking candidate, but
   must never be auto-merged:
   - An erratum/corrigendum vs. its original article (same authors/year/
     journal/volume, high title token overlap, different page).
   - A two-part study ("... Part 1" / "... Part 2": same authors/year/
     journal/volume, near-identical titles, different pages).
   - Two distinct articles by an overlapping author pair in the same
     journal issue (title-dissimilar, testing that a shared block key alone
     never causes a merge).
   - A lead author's two different papers a year apart on a related-sounding
     topic (moderate title overlap, year off by one).
3. **Noise** (8 singleton records): unrelated papers on unrelated topics,
   included so the fixture isn't *only* records designed to collide with
   something -- they should never appear as a candidate pair with anything.

`labels.json`: `duplicate_pairs` lists every pairwise combination within
each duplicate cluster (the recall/precision ground truth);
`confusable_pairs` lists the four hard-negative pairs above, purely for
documentation and reporting -- the metric computation
(`strata.dedup.benchmark.compute_metrics`) treats *any* candidate pair not
listed in `duplicate_pairs` as a ground-truth negative, so a candidate
`find_candidate_pairs` proposes that the generator didn't specifically design
is still scored correctly without needing its own label. In practice several
such candidates exist: multiple records here share enough research-methodology
vocabulary ("meta-analysis", "bias", "systematic review", ...) that the
MinHash/LSH title-blocking key (openspec:deduplication#blocking, "tuned for ~0.8 Jaccard sensitivity")
proposes them as candidates even across unrelated clusters. That is expected
and harmless: blocking is meant to cast a wide net cheaply, leaving the real
discrimination to openspec:deduplication#scoring's scoring, as long as scoring keeps these below
`review_threshold` -- which `tests/integration/test_dedup_benchmark.py`'s
false-merge-rate assertion verifies.

## Results

See `docs/dedup-benchmark-results.md` for the current numbers (regenerated by
`uv run python scripts/dedup_benchmark.py`) and
`tests/integration/test_dedup_benchmark.py` for the CI-enforced assertions
against the v1 acceptance bar (recall >= 0.95, false-merge rate <= 0.001).
